{"reply":"I understand you’d like refunds for invoices INV-0019-M4 and INV-0002-M4. Refunds are proposals, not automatic changes, and remain pending until a human approver reviews them [KB-006]. A refund request cannot be processed without that approval and must follow our standard workflow [KB-009]. Please submit a formal refund request through our support portal so it can be reviewed.", "citations":["KB-006","KB-009"]}

{"reply":"Changing from an annual Pro plan to a monthly Starter plan is a plan change, which requires authorization from an approved workspace admin and human approval [KB-014]. A downgrade normally takes effect at the next billing cycle, so the new monthly Starter subscription would start on your next renewal date unless an immediate change is requested, which could generate a prorated charge or credit [KB-012][KB-013]. Please have an authorized admin submit a plan‑change request through the billing settings, where you can select the target plan and indicate whether you want it to start now or at the next cycle [KB-011]. Our support team can explain the options but cannot apply the change without the required approval [KB-010].","citations":["KB-014","KB-012","KB-013","KB-011","KB-010"]}

{"reply":"Refunds are only possible for successful payments and must be requested within 30 days of the payment date [KB-006]. The refundable amount cannot exceed what was paid minus any prior refunds [KB-006]. If the payment for invoice INV-0005-M3 was successful and the request is within that window, we can submit a refund proposal for up to $20.02. Only one open refund request is allowed per invoice, and a human approver must approve it before any money is returned [KB-006]. Please confirm the payment date or that the payment was successful, and we’ll open a refund request for you. Do not submit another request for the same invoice while one is pending [KB-009].","citations":["KB-006","KB-009"]}

{"reply":"I can see invoice INV-0002-M2: it is paid. The successful charge was $20.01 on 21 October 2026. If you believe the amount is incorrect, our team can review the line items. Please provide the invoice ID and the specific line item you think is mis‑calculated so we can compare the plan, seat count, billing cycle, credits, and taxes with your workspace settings [KB-004].","citations":["KB-004"]}

{"reply":"I can see invoice INV-0004-M1: it is paid. The successful charge was $20.00 on 11 September 2026. The $20.00 charge you noticed on 31 October does not appear in our payment records for this invoice. To understand why you see an unexpected amount, we recommend reviewing the invoice line items and comparing them to your plan, seat count, billing cycle, credits, and taxes, as a mid‑cycle change can create a prorated charge. Support can review the disputed amount when you provide the invoice ID and the specific line item you’re questioning. [KB-004]","citations":["KB-004"]}

{"reply":"I can see invoice INV-0008-M4: it is paid. The successful charge was $20.03 on 29 October 2026; there was also a failed attempt of $10.03 on a different card. A failed payment does not affect the invoice’s paid balance, so the invoice remains marked as paid [KB-003]. If you see a charge, it corresponds to the succeeded payment shown in the record. Before retrying any payment, be sure to verify the invoice status, as an open invoice indicates no successful payment has been recorded [KB-002].","citations":["KB-003","KB-002"]}

{"reply":"Refunds are not automatic; they first appear as a pending‑approval proposal and only after a human approves are the funds transferred. If your request is still pending, please provide the refund request reference or ticket number so we can check its status [KB-009]. Refunds can only be issued for payments made within 30 days of the payment date and cannot exceed the amount that was actually paid [KB-006].", "citations":["KB-009","KB-006"]}

{"reply":"I can see invoice INV-0003-M3: it is paid. The successful charge was $20.02 on 26 September 2026. If you see a charge that seems unexpected, start by reviewing the line items on the invoice—plan, seat count, billing cycle, credits, and taxes—to see if any mid‑cycle changes caused a prorated amount [KB-004]. Each Nimbus invoice includes these details for reference [KB-001]. If after reviewing you still believe the amount is incorrect, please provide the invoice ID and the specific line item you dispute so we can investigate further.", "citations":["KB-004","KB-001"]}

{"reply":"I understand you’d like a refund for invoice INV-0006-M4. Nimbus can refund a successful payment only if the request is made within 30 days of the payment’s paid_at timestamp and the amount does not exceed the unrefunded balance [KB-006]. The invoice must have a successful payment; failed or pending payments cannot be refunded [KB-006]. Only one open refund request is allowed per invoice [KB-006]. Refunds are proposals that require human approval before any money is changed [KB-006]. I’ll submit your request for review; you’ll be notified once a decision is made.","citations":["KB-006"]}

{"reply":"Thank you for reaching out. To look into the charge on invoice INV-0003-M4, we need to compare the invoice line items with your workspace settings, as a mid‑cycle plan or seat change can create a prorated charge. Please provide the specific line item you believe was duplicated so we can review it [KB-004]. Refunds are only possible for successful payments made within the past 30 days, and the refundable amount cannot exceed the amount already paid minus any prior refunds [KB-006]. If the invoice is still open, let us know the payment confirmation so we can verify the status [KB-002]. Once we have those details we can proceed with the review.","citations":["KB-004","KB-006","KB-002"]}

{"reply":"I understand you’d like a refund for invoice INV-0004-M1. Our refund policy allows a refund only if the request is made within 30 days of the payment’s paid_at timestamp and only for the amount that was successfully paid, minus any prior refunds [KB-006]. Refund amounts are based on the actual line items shown on the invoice, not on estimates, and are limited by the successful payment and any previous refunds [KB-008]. To investigate this charge, we need to review the invoice line items and compare them with your workspace settings; please provide the specific line item you are disputing [KB-004].","citations":["KB-006","KB-008","KB-004"]}

{"reply":"Please check the Nimbus status page for any active incident; if it’s clear, retry after confirming local network access and browser console errors. Record any incident ID you see. If you use single sign‑on, be sure the configuration was tested with an administrator account before enabling enforcement and keep a verified admin login available while testing so a configuration error does not lock out the workspace. If users are locked out, have an authorized workspace administrator verify the account address or use the identity‑provider’s recovery process instead of sending password reset links. Do not enable “require SSO” until the test succeeds.", "citations":["KB-029","KB-018","KB-017"]}

{"reply":"To address the intermittent login issues, please try the following steps:
1. Use the password‑reset flow; the reset email is sent to the address on file and support will never ask for your current password or a one‑time code [KB-017].
2. If your account uses SSO, follow your identity provider’s recovery process instead of repeatedly requesting a Nimbus password reset [KB-017].
3. For multi‑factor authentication, use a saved recovery code or an existing authenticated session to update MFA; recovery codes are single‑use and should be stored offline [KB-019].
4. If you have no session or recovery code, an authorized workspace administrator must verify ownership before we can assist further [KB-019].
Let us know if you’d like to schedule a call to walk through these steps.","citations":["KB-017","KB-019"]}

{"supported": true, "conflicting": false, "reason": "Chunks provide comprehensive troubleshooting steps for sync issues", "claims": [{"claim": "Check the integration connection, last successful sync time, and whether the provider reports an outage", "kb_id": "KB-025"}, {"claim": "Verify that a workspace admin has installed the integration and has permission to change sync mappings", "kb_id": "KB-028"}, {"claim": "Review duplicate synced records and integration logs to ensure no duplicate events are causing the problem", "kb_id": "KB-026"}, {"claim": "Reconnect the integration from Settings and Integrations, granting only the required scopes and confirming the correct workspace is selected", "kb_id": "KB-024"}], "conflicting_kb_ids": []}

{"reply":"I’m sorry you’re still unable to sign in. Please try the password‑reset flow: open the Nimbus sign‑in page, choose **Forgot password**, enter your account email, and follow the link in the reset email (check spam or corporate filters if it doesn’t appear right away) [KB-017]. If the reset still fails, do not ask support for a reset link; instead have an authorized workspace administrator verify the account address, or, if you use SSO, follow your identity provider’s recovery process [KB-017].","citations":["KB-017"]}

{"reply":"Please first verify whether there is an ongoing incident on the Nimbus status page; if the page shows no active issues, try signing in again after confirming local network access [KB-029]. If the problem persists, use the password‑reset flow: open the sign‑in page, select Forgot password, enter the account email, follow the reset link from the newest email, and choose a new password that you haven’t used elsewhere [KB-017]. Ensure the reset email isn’t filtered to spam and that the address is correct; if the account uses SSO, follow your identity provider’s recovery process instead of requesting another Nimbus password reset [KB-017]. Let us know the outcome or any error messages you see.","citations":["KB-029","KB-017"]}

{"supported": true, "conflicting": false, "reason": "Retrieved chunks contain troubleshooting steps for sync issues", "claims": [{"claim": "Check the integration connection, last successful sync time, and whether the provider reports an outage; record the error before reconnecting", "kb_id": "KB-025"}, {"claim": "Review duplicate synced records by checking external object IDs and event history, and avoid bulk-deleting records", "kb_id": "KB-026"}], "conflicting_kb_ids": []}

{"reply":"First, please verify that there is no ongoing Nimbus incident by checking the status page and note any incident ID you see [KB-029]. If the status page is clear, confirm the integration connection: open Settings → Integrations, ensure the provider is connected to the correct workspace and that the required scopes are granted [KB-024]. Also check the last successful sync time and whether the provider reports an outage; record any error details before reconnecting [KB-025]. If you see duplicate records, review the external object ID and event history rather than bulk‑deleting [KB-026]. Finally, make sure a workspace admin has granted the necessary permissions for the integration [KB-028]. Let us know what you find, and we can investigate further.", "citations":["KB-029","KB-024","KB-025","KB-026","KB-028"]}

{"reply":"To address the data inconsistencies, start by checking the integration connection, the last successful sync time, and whether the provider reports an outage [KB-025]. Review the integration logs and a sample external object ID to see if duplicate records were created by a retry or overlapping mappings; avoid bulk‑deleting records and investigate individual objects instead [KB-026]. If the sync remains delayed, provide the integration name, affected object type, and approximate start time to support [KB-025]. Should you need to move data, you can export records from Settings and Data export and re‑import using the documented template with stable external IDs to prevent duplicates [KB-027].","citations":["KB-025","KB-026","KB-027"]}

{"reply":"To troubleshoot the sync between Monday.com and Airtable, please try the following steps:
1. Verify the integration connection and note the last successful sync time; check if the provider reports any outage. Reconnect only after recording the error and confirming the correct workspace is selected [KB-025].
2. Ensure a workspace admin has installed the integration and that sync mappings are set correctly, as only admins can change these settings [KB-028].
3. Review the integration logs for duplicate records. If duplicates appear, check the external object ID and event history before deleting anything; avoid bulk‑deleting records [KB-026].
4. If the connection still fails, go to Settings → Integrations, select the provider, grant the requested scopes, and confirm the integration is linked to the intended workspace [KB-024].
If the issue persists after these steps, please provide the integration name, affected object type, and the approximate time the problem started so we can investigate further.","citations":["KB-025","KB-028","KB-026","KB-024"]}

{"reply":"To troubleshoot the sync issue, first verify the integration connection and the time of the last successful sync, and check if the provider is reporting an outage. Record any error messages and confirm you are using the correct workspace before attempting a reconnect [KB-025]. If the integration was recently installed or its settings changed, ensure that a workspace admin has granted the necessary permissions, as only admins can modify sync mappings [KB-028]. When reviewing the data, look for duplicate records that can appear if an event was retried; avoid bulk‑deleting and instead check the external object ID and event history before making changes [KB-026]. If the connection itself failed, revisit Settings → Integrations, select the provider, grant only the requested scopes, and confirm the integration is linked to the intended workspace [KB-024].","citations":["KB-025","KB-028","KB-026","KB-024"]}

{"reply":"To troubleshoot the Smartsheet‑Azure failure, first verify that a workspace admin installed the integration and that you have the needed permissions, as only admins can change integration settings [KB-028]. Then go to Settings → Integrations, select the Azure provider, and ensure only the requested scopes are granted; confirm the integration is linked to the correct workspace before syncing [KB-024]. If the connection still fails, capture the provider name and any error code and share those details with support [KB-024]. Also make sure any API keys used are created by a workspace admin, stored securely, and not exposed in tickets [KB-021].","citations":["KB-028","KB-024","KB-021"]}

{"supported": true, "conflicting": false, "reason": "Chunks provide upgrade procedure and next-cycle details", "claims": [{"claim": "A workspace admin can request an upgrade from Settings → Billing → Change plan.", "kb_id": "KB-011"}, {"claim": "When upgrading, you must specify the current plan (Starter) and target plan (Pro) and choose the effective date as the next billing cycle.", "kb_id": "KB-011"}, {"claim": "A next-cycle upgrade will not incur a prorated charge; the change takes effect at the start of the next billing period.", "kb_id": "KB-013"}], "conflicting_kb_ids": []}

{"reply":"To upgrade from Starter to Pro you’ll need to be a workspace admin. In Settings → Billing → Change plan you can select the Pro plan, review its features and seat limits, and choose the effective date. Since you want the upgrade to start at the next billing cycle, select that option when submitting the request. The upgrade proposal must identify the current and target plans and the effective date; the displayed estimate is not final – the actual invoice will reflect the change [KB-011]. A next‑cycle change will not affect the current invoice period [KB-013]. If you need help submitting the request, please let us know.","citations":["KB-011","KB-013"]}

{"supported":true,"conflicting":false,"reason":"Chunks provide refund policy and cancellation info to explain eligibility and process.","claims":[{"claim":"Cancellation does not automatically result in a refund.","kb_id":"KB-015"},{"claim":"Refunds are only possible within 30 days of the successful payment and cannot exceed the amount paid minus any prior refunds.","kb_id":"KB-006"},{"claim":"Support must verify the invoice belongs to the customer, the payment status, and that the request is within the 30‑day window before processing a refund.","kb_id":"KB-006"}],"conflicting_kb_ids":[]}

{"reply":"Thank you for your request. According to our policy, a refund is a proposal that must receive recorded human approval before any money is changed [KB-006]. A refund request can be pending approval, approved, rejected, executed, or failed, and you should submit a ticket with the refund reference rather than trying to bypass the process [KB-009]. Every refund still requires a human approver, even if you are a billing admin [KB-007]. Our team will review your request and get back to you with the next steps.", "citations":["KB-006","KB-009","KB-007"]}

{"reply":"Thank you for reaching out. Canceling a workspace does not automatically generate a refund; a refund requires eligibility checks [KB-015]. Nimbus can refund a successful payment only if the request is made within 30 days of the payment’s paid_at timestamp and the amount does not exceed the unrefunded portion of the original payment [KB-006]. We will need to verify that invoice INV-0005-M1 has a successful payment and that the request falls within the 30‑day window before proceeding [KB-006]. If the payment qualifies, the refundable amount will be based on the actual payment recorded, not the plan price alone [KB-008]. Please allow us some time to review the invoice and payment details, and we will get back to you with the outcome.","citations":["KB-015","KB-006","KB-008"]}
